title: Greek Fire
sentences: The Byzantines had a weapon that kept burning on water, and its recipe is lost.
It is called Greek fire, and it was first used in the 670s, when Arab fleets threatened Constantinople.
Crews sprayed it through tubes mounted on their ships.
Water did not put it out, and old accounts say only sand, vinegar or urine could.
The formula was a closely guarded state secret.
Historians think it was based on petroleum, but no one knows the exact recipe.
